parameters.content:

Upload TICKET-<id>.pdf. An optional TICKET-<id>.jpg must arrive first to be included. A lone photo prompts a report reminder. Explicit FM approval closes the ticket; rejection requests rework. parameters.query:
SELECT t.*,
 t.description AS damage_description,t.ifc_name AS object_type,t.photo_before_url AS photo_url,
 te.full_name AS technician_name,te.email AS technician_email,
 coalesce(substring(t.photo_before_url from '/d/([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)'),substring(t.photo_before_url from '[?&]id=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)')) AS before_file_id
 FROM tickets t LEFT JOIN technicians te ON te.id=t.technician_id WHERE t.id=$1 LIMIT 1;

parameters.text:
=You are the quality-verification engine of a facility-maintenance system.
Image 1 is the BEFORE photo of a reported issue: {{ $('Fetch Ticket').item.json.damage_description }} (object: {{ $('Fetch Ticket').item.json.object_type }}).
Image 2 is the AFTER photo uploaded by the technician who claims the repair is complete.

Compare the two images and respond with ONLY a minified JSON object, no markdown fences: {"repair_verified": true or false, "confidence": number between 0 and 1, "observations": one short factual sentence}.
repair_verified is true only if Image 2 plausibly shows the same object with the reported issue resolved.

parameters.query:
UPDATE tickets SET status='PENDING_APPROVAL',report_text=$2,report_file_id=$3,after_file_id=$4,
 verification=$5::jsonb,approval_id=gen_random_uuid(),ifc_new_version=NULL,updated_at=clock_timestamp()
 WHERE id=$1 AND status IN ('ASSIGNED','WORK_DONE','REWORK') AND technician_id IS NOT NULL
 RETURNING id,status,approval_id;

parameters.text: ={{ "Carry out the persisted FM decision. Bound context: " + JSON.stringify($("Closure Context").first().json) }}

options.systemMessage:
You are the closure supervisor for WF2. The facility manager has already decided; your job is to carry that decision out against the database, the IFC service and email, and to recover from failures that a fixed node chain could not.

Complete every objective listed in the bound context, in a sensible order. For an APPROVED decision: write the maintenance record to the IFC model, close the ticket recording the returned model version, increment the technician's completed-jobs count, then notify the technician and the facility manager. For a REJECTED decision: reopen the ticket for rework and notify the technician what is required.

ATTEMPT BUDGET: you may attempt any single operation at most 3 times. When a tool returns an error, do not simply repeat the identical call. Read the error. If it names a missing column, a type mismatch or an unknown relation, call inspect_schema to see the columns that actually exist, then retry with corrected arguments. If the error is a timeout or a transient connection failure, one plain retry is reasonable. If an operation still fails after 3 attempts, stop attempting it, continue with the remaining objectives that do not depend on it, and report precisely which objective failed and why.

The database tools run fixed parameterized statements and are idempotent: closing an already closed ticket, or reopening an already reopened one, is safe and reports no rows changed. Email is NOT idempotent. Send each notification once. Before re-sending after an uncertain result, call check_notice to see whether that notice was already recorded as sent.

You cannot execute free-form SQL and you cannot choose a different ticket: the workflow binds the ticket identity. inspect_schema is read-only and exists solely to diagnose a failure.

Finish with a short structured summary naming each objective and whether it succeeded, the number of attempts it took, and the exact error for anything that failed. Your summary is a report, not proof: the workflow verifies committed database state independently.
Approval timeout never authorizes rework. Rejection reasons are fixed by context; never invent one. log_ifc_maintenance uses a guarded helper and persists the real service result before close_ticket. An absent element is recorded as SKIPPED. On service failure the helper records CBM_WF2_ATTEMPT; close_ticket retains NULL. FM notifications read committed database state; never claim IFC updated without a successful result. All ticket mutations require the same persisted approval identity.

parameters.query:
SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type, is_nullable
  FROM information_schema.columns
 WHERE table_schema = 'public'
   AND table_name IN ('tickets','technicians','ticket_events')
 ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position;
parameters.toolDescription: Read-only. Returns the columns and types that actually exist on the tickets, technicians and ticket_events tables. Call this when a tool error names a missing column, an unknown relation or a type mismatch, then retry the failed operation with corrected arguments. Cannot modify anything.

parameters.name: log_ifc_maintenance
parameters.description: Apply the approved IFC write using the bound operation key. Skips missing elements. Persists the real success/failure. Safe to retry the same operation key.

parameters.query: WITH v AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS p) UPDATE tickets SET status='CLOSED',closed_at=clock_timestamp(),updated_at=clock_timestamp() FROM v WHERE tickets.id=(v.p->>'ticketId')::int AND tickets.status='PENDING_APPROVAL' AND tickets.approval_id=(v.p->>'approvalId')::uuid AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM ticket_events e WHERE e.ticket_id=tickets.id AND e.event='CBM_WF2_APPROVAL' AND e.payload->>'approval_id'=v.p->>'approvalId' AND e.payload->>'decision'='APPROVED') AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM ticket_events e WHERE e.ticket_id=tickets.id AND e.event IN ('CBM_WF2_IFC_RESULT','CBM_WF2_ATTEMPT') AND e.payload->>'operation_key'=v.p->>'operationKey') RETURNING tickets.id,tickets.status,tickets.closed_at,tickets.ifc_new_version;
parameters.toolDescription: Close after the guarded IFC helper recorded success, failure or skip. The database retains its verified model version; failure stays NULL. Requires the current persisted APPROVED decision.

parameters.query: WITH v AS (SELECT $1::jsonb AS p) UPDATE tickets SET status='REWORK',closed_at=NULL,fm_reject_reason=v.p->>'rejectionReason',updated_at=clock_timestamp() FROM v WHERE tickets.id=(v.p->>'ticketId')::int AND tickets.status='PENDING_APPROVAL' AND tickets.approval_id=(v.p->>'approvalId')::uuid AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM ticket_events e WHERE e.ticket_id=tickets.id AND e.event='CBM_WF2_APPROVAL' AND e.payload->>'approval_id'=v.p->>'approvalId' AND e.payload->>'decision'='REJECTED') RETURNING tickets.id,tickets.status;
parameters.toolDescription: Reopen the bound ticket for rework after a rejected approval, recording the facility manager's reason. Idempotent: a ticket already in REWORK reports zero rows changed.

parameters.query:
WITH receipt AS (
 INSERT INTO ticket_events(ticket_id,event,payload) SELECT id,'CBM_WF2_STATS',jsonb_build_object('approval_id',approval_id)
 FROM tickets WHERE id=($1::jsonb->>'ticketId')::int AND status='CLOSED' AND approval_id=($1::jsonb->>'approvalId')::uuid
 ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING ticket_id)
 UPDATE technicians SET jobs_completed=jobs_completed+1 WHERE id IN (SELECT technician_id FROM tickets WHERE id IN (SELECT ticket_id FROM receipt)) RETURNING id,jobs_completed;
parameters.toolDescription: Increment the assigned technician's completed-jobs counter. Call once, after close_ticket succeeds. Reports zero rows changed if the ticket has no assigned technician.

parameters.query:
SELECT payload->>'notice_key' AS notice_key, created_at
  FROM ticket_events
 WHERE ticket_id = ($1::jsonb->>'ticketId')::int AND event = 'CBM_WF2_NOTICE'
 ORDER BY id;
parameters.toolDescription: Return the notices already recorded as sent for the bound ticket. Call this before re-sending an email whose result was uncertain, so a technician or the facility manager is not notified twice.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO ticket_events(ticket_id, event, payload)
SELECT ($1::jsonb->>'ticketId')::int,
       CASE WHEN upper($1::jsonb->>'kind')='NOTICE'
            THEN 'CBM_WF2_NOTICE' ELSE 'CBM_WF2_ATTEMPT' END,
       jsonb_build_object('notice_key', $1::jsonb->>'key',
                          'operation',  $1::jsonb->>'operation',
                          'outcome',    $1::jsonb->>'outcome',
                          'detail',     $1::jsonb->>'detail')
RETURNING id, event;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [JSON.stringify({ ticketId: $("Closure Context").first().json.ticketId, kind: $fromAI("kind", "NOTICE for a delivered email, ATTEMPT for an operation outcome", "string"), key: $fromAI("notice_key", "Stable key of the notice, for example technician:closed or fm:closed or technician:rework. Empty for ATTEMPT", "string"), operation: $fromAI("operation", "Name of the tool or objective this record concerns", "string"), outcome: $fromAI("outcome", "SUCCEEDED or FAILED", "string"), detail: $fromAI("detail", "Exact error text when it failed, otherwise a short note", "string") })] }}

parameters.toolDescription: Record one operation attempt or one delivered notice in the append-only audit trail. Set kind to NOTICE immediately after an email is sent successfully, using the notice key you sent; set it to ATTEMPT to record a failed operation and its error. This is what makes retries auditable.

parameters.subject: ={{ "Ticket " + $("Closure Context").first().json.ticketId + " - " + ($("Closure Context").first().json.decision === "APPROVED" ? "approved and closed" : "rework required") }}
parameters.message: ={{ "Ticket #" + $("Closure Context").first().json.ticketId + ": " + ($("Closure Context").first().json.decision === "APPROVED" ? "The facility manager approved your completion." : $("Closure Context").first().json.rejectionReason + " Contact the facility manager for details, then upload a revised TICKET-" + $("Closure Context").first().json.ticketId + ".pdf.") }}
parameters.toolDescription: Email the assigned technician. Use it once for an approved closure and once for a rejected completion; write the body to suit which happened. Record it with record_attempt kind=NOTICE afterwards.

parameters.name: notify_fm
parameters.description: Notify the FM from the committed CLOSED ticket. Subject and model result are fixed by database state. Records delivery; stops for manual reconciliation if a delivery result is uncertain.

parameters.query: SELECT id,status,closed_at,ifc_new_version,(SELECT count(*) FROM ticket_events WHERE ticket_id=t.id AND event='CBM_WF2_NOTICE') AS notices_recorded,(SELECT count(*) FROM ticket_events WHERE ticket_id=t.id AND event='CBM_WF2_ATTEMPT') AS attempts_recorded FROM tickets t WHERE id=$1;

parameters.subject: =[CBM] Written report required for ticket #{{ $("Fetch Ticket").first().json.id }}
parameters.message: =Your photo was received. To submit completion, upload your written report as TICKET-{{ $("Fetch Ticket").first().json.id }}.pdf to the completed folder. The photo alone does not request approval.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO ticket_events(ticket_id,event,payload)
 SELECT id,'CBM_WF2_APPROVAL_EXPIRED',jsonb_build_object('approval_id',approval_id,'status','PENDING_APPROVAL')
 FROM tickets WHERE id=$1 AND status='PENDING_APPROVAL' AND approval_id=$2::uuid
 RETURNING ticket_id;

INSERT INTO ticket_events(ticket_id,event,payload)
 SELECT id,'CBM_WF2_APPROVAL',jsonb_build_object('approval_id',approval_id,'decision',$3::text)
 FROM tickets WHERE id=$1 AND approval_id=$2::uuid AND status='PENDING_APPROVAL'
 AND $3 IN ('APPROVED','REJECTED')
 AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM ticket_events WHERE ticket_id=$1 AND event='CBM_WF2_APPROVAL' AND payload->>'approval_id'=$2::text)
 RETURNING ticket_id;
